description: Set the value of ball thermal attributes. This command is a synonym for the ball thermal initialize command. Individual attributes can be listed with the ball thermal list command, and all ball thermal attributes can be visualized.

python_sdk_alternative.workaround: itasca.ball.thermal.find(id) then set_temp()/set_expansion()/set_specific_heat()/set_power_app()/set_del_temp() per object - iterate for ranges

keywords.name: temperature-increment
keywords.description: temperature increment since last mechanical coupling

keywords.name: gradient
keywords.description: Apply a linear gradient in each of the axes directions starting at the origin; the stored value is the base value plus gradient dot position.

examples.description: Set the temperature of all thermal balls
Base temperature plus a linear gradient from the origin (value = 100 + 2x + 3y)

notes: The 7.0/9.0 manuals attach a post-value modifier block (add, gradient, gradient-x/y/z, multiply, replace) to every attribute; live, only plain 'gradient <v>' is accepted - add, multiply, replace and the gradient-x/y/z spellings are rejected on 6.00, 7.00 and 9.8 (2D and 3D). The 6.0 manual does not document the block, but 6.00 accepts 'gradient' all the same.
Thermal attributes are characteristics of the thermal balls (such as temperature or power); they are distinct from the surface properties assigned with 'ball thermal property'.
verification: Live-verified 2026-11-09 on PFC2D and PFC3D 6.00, 7.00 and 9.8 consoles (state grade): expansion, power-applied, specific-heat, temperature and temperature-increment each set and read back exactly via ball.thermal.* FISH intrinsics on all six consoles; gradient read back as base value plus gradient dot position (the ball at the origin stays at the base value).
